findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — parseRefreshTokenResponse's return contract changed from a parsed object to a full zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper, but this call still assigns the wrapper directly to `key` and persists it as `credential.key`, corrupting every Google Calendar OAuth refresh regardless of whether credential sync is enabled

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:8 — minimumTokenResponseSchema uses `[z.string().toString()]` as a computed object key, which evaluates once to the static string "[object Object]" instead of matching arbitrary field names, so safeParse silently strips every response field except access_token (verified empirically with zod) whenever the new credential-sync path is active

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — Fallback sets refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token" (not a real token value) whenever the parsed response lacks one, which — combined with the field-stripping bug above — will corrupt stored refresh tokens for any provider using this helper while credential sync is enabled

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:98 — Because parseRefreshTokenResponse switches schema based on a global APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED/CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT flag rather than whether this specific response came from the sync endpoint, enabling credential sync strips instance_url, token_type, scope, signature and issued_at from Salesforce's response before it's persisted, even though Salesforce always calls Salesforce's own token endpoint directly — breaking salesforceTokenSchema-shaped downstream consumers (e.g. jsforce.Connection instanceUrl)

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — When routed through CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT this returns the raw, unparsed fetch Response, but the Google CalendarService caller (CalendarService.ts:94, `res?.data`) expects a gaxios-style object with a pre-parsed `.data` field like the non-sync branch returns, so `token` will be undefined and `token.access_token` throws

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — Request body is validated with zod `.parse()` (throws) instead of `.safeParse()`, and the handler has no try/catch or defaultHandler/defaultResponder wrapper (unlike sibling app-store api routes in this same diff), so a malformed payload produces an unhandled exception and an opaque framework 500 instead of a well-formed 400 with a useful error body for external integrators

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:81 — Create and update both return HTTP 200 with only a free-text `message` string distinguishing the outcome (no `created`/`updated` boolean, no resource id, no schema version), giving external integrators nothing stable to branch on programmatically

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:1 — New public webhook has no API versioning story at all (no /v1/ path segment, no version field in request or response) despite being explicitly designed per .env.example for long-term third-party self-hoster integrations

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:1 — The `{ userId, appSlug, keys }` request contract and its response shapes are documented only in .env.example comments; no README or API doc ships alongside this new externally-consumed endpoint

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — Handler has no HTTP method guard, so non-POST requests fall through to the same body-parsing logic (and same opaque 500 on missing body) instead of a clean 405 Method Not Allowed

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:3 — decodeOAuthState/encodeOAuthState import IntegrationOAuthCallbackState from "../../types", but this checkout contains no packages/app-store/types.ts, so drift between the decoded/encoded state shape and its type could not be verified in this review environment

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192 — in credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response instead of a parsed HubspotToken, so `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` are undefined, producing `expiryDate: NaN` at line 192 and silently persisting a corrupted HubSpot credential key (no exception is thrown, so the surrounding try/catch never logs it)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:50 — appStoreMetadata is indexed by `app.slug`, but elsewhere in this same diff an app's slug can differ from its appStoreMetadata object key (e.g. office365video is registered under slug "msteams" per its own createOAuthAppCredential call), so this lookup returns undefined and the webhook 404s for any app whose config slug differs from its appStoreMetadata key

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — refreshFunction: () => any` lets the two branches return incompatible shapes (raw un-.json()'d fetch Response from the sync endpoint vs. whatever the caller's refreshFunction returns, e.g. a client-SDK object), so the helper doesn't unify anything and every call site still needs provider-specific unwrapping, with no compile-time check that it does so correctly

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:246 — The `async () => await fetch(...)` refreshFunction wrapper required by refreshOAuthTokens is repeated near-verbatim boilerplate across office365calendar/office365video/webex/larkcalendar/hubspot; the indirection doesn't reduce the (legitimately provider-specific) duplication of URL/params, it only adds a callback layer over what used to be a plain awaited fetch
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:16 — Empty `/** */` JSDoc comment directly above the handler is dead/meaningless and should be removed

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8 — fetch() to the operator-controlled CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT has no timeout/AbortController, no retry, and no try/catch, so a hung or unreachable sync endpoint blocks OAuth refresh (and the booking/calendar-sync flow calling it) indefinitely across every provider now routed through it

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5 — When a credential belongs to a team (credential.userId is null), refreshOAuthTokens silently bypasses CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and falls back to direct provider refresh with no logging, leaving an unexplained failure path for team-owned integrations when operators rely solely on credential sync

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:84 — responseBody.expiry_date is recomputed from responseBody.expires_in (defaulting to 0) even when the response came from the credential-sync endpoint, whose documented contract only guarantees access_token/expiry, so a sync response without expires_in overwrites expiry to "now" and forces a refresh (hitting the sync endpoint) on every subsequent request

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — New public webhook decrypts attacker-supplied ciphertext and writes credentials for arbitrary userId, but ships with zero tests for secret-mismatch->403, missing-user->404, missing-app->404, malformed-ciphertext decrypt, create-vs-update branch, and sharing-disabled->403.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — When the credential-sync branch of refreshOAuthTokens is taken, res is a raw fetch Response with no .data property, so `res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws on the next line; untested.

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192 — When the credential-sync branch is taken, hubspotRefreshToken is a raw fetch Response (not a HubspotToken), so `.expiresIn` is undefined, `expiryDate` becomes NaN, and a malformed credential is persisted via prisma; untested.

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — New unconditional token-refresh path in getClient() calls `prisma.credential.update` but `prisma` is never imported in this file, so every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation throws a ReferenceError at runtime; a trivial unit test would have caught this immediately.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1 — No test files exist anywhere in the repo for the CalendarService/VideoApiAdapter classes touched by this PR (googlecalendar, hubspot, office365calendar, salesforce, webex), so the new refreshOAuthTokens wrapping is a pre-existing coverage gap rather than ignored test infra; the pruned repo snapshot (only the 30 diffed files) limits full verification against the project's real test history.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

However, calling this a “real problem” is not objectively verifiable from the diff alone: there is no contract/spec in the diff requiring stable machine-readable fields, and returning a simple message string is not inherently a bug, security issue, or correctness defect. It’s an API design suggestion rather than a clear defect introduced by the change.

However, the proposed finding is about the absence of a README/API doc, which is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness defect in the code shown—it's a documentation/process expectation that cannot be strictly confirmed from this diff alone (the repo may document it elsewhere, or may not require such docs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — Handler has no HTTP method guard, so non-POST requests fall through to the same body-parsing logic (and same opaque 500 on missing body) instead of a clean 405 Method Not Allowed

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the exported handler never checks req.method (e.g., POST-only). After the secret checks, it unconditionally runs `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`. For non-POST requests (GET/HEAD/etc.), `req.body` is typically undefined/empty, so Zod `.parse` will throw and the route will return a generic 500 rather than a clean 405 Method Not Allowed (or at least a controlled 4xx). This is directly verifiable in the added file; there is no method guard or try/catch around parsing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192 — in credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response instead of a parsed HubspotToken, so `.expiresIn`/`.accessToken` are undefined, producing `expiryDate: NaN` at line 192 and silently persisting a corrupted HubSpot credential key (no exception is thrown, so the surrounding try/catch never logs it)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now assigns `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. But `refreshOAuthTokens` (new file) returns **either** the result of `refreshFunction()` (a `HubspotToken` in the non-sync path) **or** a raw `fetch(...)` return value (a `Response`) in credential-sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`). The HubSpot service code shown does not parse the `Response` (e.g., `await response.json()`) before treating it as `HubspotToken`, so in sync mode the returned value will not have HubSpot token fields (e.g., `expiresIn`, `accessToken`), leading to undefined values being used downstream. This type/behavior mismatch is directly introduced by the diff and is a concrete correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:50 — appStoreMetadata is indexed by `app.slug`, but elsewhere in this same diff an app's slug can differ from its appStoreMetadata object key (e.g. office365video is registered under slug "msteams" per its own createOAuthAppCredential call), so this lookup returns undefined and the webhook 404s for any app whose config slug differs from its appStoreMetadata key

adjudication.rationale: The webhook handler looks up metadata via `appStoreMetadata[app.slug]`, where `app.slug` comes from the `App` row fetched by `prisma.app.findUnique({ where: { slug: reqBody.appSlug } })`. The proposed finding claims there are apps whose DB slug differs from the `appStoreMetadata` key (e.g. “office365video” vs “msteams”), but the diff does not show any evidence of such a mismatch: it does not include `appStoreMetadata` contents, any `App` records, nor any place where `office365video` is “registered under” a different slug. The only concrete “msteams” string in the diff is passed to `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`, which is used for an external credential-sync refresh endpoint and does not prove the Prisma `app.slug` differs from the `appStoreMetadata` key. Therefore the claimed undefined lookup/404 cannot be verified from this diff and is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3 — refreshFunction: () => any` lets the two branches return incompatible shapes (raw un-.json()'d fetch Response from the sync endpoint vs. whatever the caller's refreshFunction returns, e.g. a client-SDK object), so the helper doesn't unify anything and every call site still needs provider-specific unwrapping, with no compile-time check that it does so correctly

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, the sync branch does `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response`, while the non-sync branch returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns (often an already-parsed object, e.g. HubspotToken, or a Gaxios response with `.data`). The call sites shown in the diff assume provider-specific shapes: e.g. Google Calendar does `const token = res?.data;` (works for GaxiosResponse, but not for a fetch `Response`), and Hubspot types the result as `HubspotToken` (but would receive a fetch `Response` under the sync branch). Since the helper is typed `() => any` and returns `any`, TypeScript won’t catch these mismatches, and at runtime the sync configuration would break token refresh handling unless every caller adds special unwrapping/parsing.
